Village on moon: European Space Agency's distant dream
Unfortunately it's probs just another well meaning European pipe dream :(
I don't see the purpose of it, if you can do it on Mars then do it on Mars .

Because it is the ultimate frontier for the current technology , science will be much more exciting since moon is a piece of earth , it has an abundance of water and everybody wants a manned Mars mission . Yes i understand that the distance is longer , it has sandstorms , strange pressure and other environmental hazards but in the slim chance fossilized microbial life is discovered our entire perspective of the universe will change dramatically .

I don't agree with pushing frontiers with expensive projects just for the sake of it, that money could potentially be put to much better uses. As for everyone wanting a manned mars mission... maybe. But do they want to pay for it? And do they want it more than they want their local hospital not to close?

Discovering microbial life would be cool, but it wouldn't really change much. It's not an intelligent being we could converse with, or even macrofauna we could interact with and it's almost certain that life exists elsewhere in the universe anyhow.

If we're going to push boundaries in space I think the focus should be on making launch technology cheaper and more accessible rather than sending two or three people somewhere there's no real demand for them to be. Even a moon base I'd be happy holding off on until regular people can get into orbit.

The hardest part of space flight currently is getting things launched off of Earth - it becomes exponentially harder and costly the further into the solar system we go. If we can construct a base to first harvest fuel and then construct space craft, it would significantly reduce the cost of space exploration. Couple that with some amazing science experiments and faster emergency response times to/from earth and the moon doesn't look like a bad jump point to the rest of the solar system. I don't think a moon base is an end goal. It's a stepping stone to bigger things.
If the idea is to make some kind of a construction site this can be done in orbit, no need to take it 3 days away .

you still need to escape earth gravity well, witch is much easier if you do it from the moon. If you can construct a spaceship with fuel an everything completely in moons orbit, you just need a little push to escape velocity. Much less than from earth orbit.

The most awesome thing would be a space elevator. A space station in geostationary orbit with a cable down to earth. As a counterweight you just extend the cable witch can be used to achieve escape velocity without burning any fuel.

Look, I am aging and by the time that I die I really want to have visited an alien place. If I have to wait for Mars then I probably will need to reincarnate twice.

Building a place on the Moon means touristic shuttles will follow.
